newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 28.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The military and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front signed yesterday an initial accord to end their fierce gunbattle in Buldon, Maguindanao, that have left heavy casualties and displaced thousands of families. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The Palace will create a five-member regulatory panel to oversee and protect public interest in the operations of the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System which will be transferred shortly to the hands of concessionaires. (STAR/CHRONICLE)
- President Fidel Ramos yesterday called for a total modernization of the electoral process to reduce the incidence of fraud and make it efficient and credible. (CHRONICLE/STANDARD/STAR)

- The Committee on Privatisation is readying the sale of another government-owned utility firm, National Power Corp, by the last quarter of this year after the successful bidding of Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System last week, Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The Court of Appeals yesterday upheld a Board of Investments ruling approving JG Summit Petrochemical Corp's decision to establish a petrochemical plant in Batangas city. (BUSINESSWORLD/TIMES)

- About 10 billion pesos worth of investments will be withdrawn should the government scrap incentives to industrial estate projects in Laguna and Cavite under the 1997 Investment Priorities Plan. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
